name: Post-processed Raman reference library of 79 ocean polymer specimens (61 anthropogenic polymers + 18 biological materials), 200-3,400 cm^-1 (Miller et al. 2022, Scientific Data 9:780)
description: Post-processed Raman spectra of 79 ocean polymer specimens from the open-access reference library of Miller et al. 2022 (Scientific Data 9, 780, doi:10.1038/s41597-022-01883-5; data: OSF project https://osf.io/7cqv4/). The library covers (a) 40 pristine anthropogenic polymers newly sourced from manufacturers, (b) 22 weathered anthropogenic polymers from used consumer, beachcast, agricultural and fishery sources, and (c) 17 biological polymers representing diverse marine taxa, trophic levels and tissues; the deposit holds 18 BIOL-coded specimens (the 17 biological materials plus a charcoal reference, which is carbonaceous, not a polymer). The 79 spectra (61 PLAS-coded + 18 BIOL-coded particles, one per specimen) carry the authors' uniform 3,201-point 200-3,400 cm^-1 @1 cm^-1 grid and are peak-normalized (max = 1.0, min = 0) as deposited. The deposit's long-format CSV (Data2_processed.csv, one row per spectrum-wavenumber point) is pivoted here; no further preprocessing is applied. Task: classification by the deposit's poly_lab label - 59 classes, of which 12 have replicates (bone x4, PETE x4, PP x4, PS x3, chitin x3, cellulose x3, HDPE x2, myofibrillar protein x2, PA x2, PE x2, calcium carbonate x2) and 47 are singleton reference entries, so most classes are single-spectrum references; the coarse plastic-vs-biological split (61 vs 18) is derivable from the labels. is_grouped=False (one spectrum per specimen). The deposit's raw measurement files (87 spectra, 532/780 nm excitation, repeat measurements) are served separately as the ocean_polymers_raw key. License note: the OSF project page sets no explicit license; the open-access parent paper (CC BY 4.0) publishes these data records in its Data Records section, which is the license used here.

rai:dataCollection: Raman measurements of 79 ocean polymer specimens (61 anthropogenic polymer particles, 18 biological material specimens) recorded for the reference library; the authors' post-processed grid (200-3,400 cm^-1 @1 cm^-1, 3,201 points) and peak normalization are as deposited.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Applied by the authors as deposited: resampling onto the uniform 200-3,400 cm^-1 @1 cm^-1 grid (3,201 points) and peak normalization to max = 1.0 (min = 0). The raman_data loader only pivots the long-format CSV (one row per spectrum-wavenumber point) into wide spectra; no baseline correction, smoothing or further normalization is applied.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Labels are the deposit's own poly_lab assignments (polymer codes such as PETE/PP/PS/HDPE for the anthropogenic specimens; tissue or material names such as bone, chitin, cellulose, keratin for the biological ones; a few descriptive strings for weathered items such as 'beachcast white foam sheet' or 'strawberry container'); no re-labelling was performed for this benchmark.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included. All samples are polymer specimens and biological marine materials (bones, chitin, tissues, etc.).
rai:dataBiases: Reference-library design: 47 of the 59 poly_lab classes are singleton entries (one spectrum), so the key supports spectral matching and few-shot use more than large-scale CV classification; only 12 classes have replicates (bone x4, PETE x4, PP x4, PS x3, chitin x3, cellulose x3, HDPE x2, myofibrillar protein x2, PA x2, PE x2, calcium carbonate x2). Spectra are peak-normalized 0-1, removing absolute intensity information; the spectra mix pristine, weathered and biological specimens, and the weathered items carry only coarse descriptive labels.
rai:dataLimitations: Most classes are single-spectrum references (47 of 59); peak normalization removes absolute intensity information; the 200-3,400 cm^-1 window excludes the low-wavenumber region below 200 cm^-1; weathered specimens carry coarse descriptive labels rather than polymer codes; one charcoal specimen is coded as biological (BIOL) although it is carbonaceous, not a polymer; the OSF project sets no explicit license (the open-access paper's CC BY 4.0 is applied).
rai:dataSocialImpact: Supports marine plastic pollution research: identifying the material of marine debris (plastic vs biological) where visual techniques are not diagnostic; environmental monitoring use, no human or medical data.
rai:dataUseCases: Reference spectra for polymer identification of ocean debris (spectral matching, few-shot / augmentation); plastic-vs-biological discrimination (61 vs 18 spectra, derivable from the labels); limited as a large-scale CV classification benchmark because most classes are singletons.
